parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description:
Caller-generated unique key (a UUID per logical submit) that makes a
retried request safe: 1 to 128 printable ASCII characters. Every POST
needs it, in every deployment (the service always runs on Postgres; there
is no in-memory mode). An absent key is a 400 `idempotency-key-required`,
an invalid one (longer than 128 characters or
with a control or non-ASCII character) is a 400 `idempotency-key-invalid`.
A replay with the same key and the same method, path and body returns the
stored response (status, headers and body) with `Idempotency-Replayed:
true`, but only when the first answer was final for the request: a 2xx
and a FINAL refusal are stored and replayed, while a RETRYABLE refusal
(409 `approved-plan-conflict`, 409 `concurrent-modification`, 400
`invalid-site-id` when no default site is configured) is not stored --
its key is released and the retry executes the work again, so the same
key with a different body afterwards is a NEW request, not a conflict.
The same key with a different request against a STORED answer is
409 `idempotency-key-reused`. A 5xx outcome is never stored.
